newsitem.title: UK: Total progressing on Iran S.Pars study.
newsitem.headline: Total progressing on Iran S.Pars study.

text.p: French giant Total said it was seriously weighing the option of investing in Iran's giant South Pars gas field and would not be deterred by the threat of U.S. sanctions, an official said on Thursday.

The official referred to remarks by Total chairman Thierry Desmarast at a news conference in which he said that the company was studying the project. He said this was the first confirmation by Total of its interest in South Pars.

"These are not small projects...We are looking to take decisions after assembling the maximum of elements to evaluate on the one hand, the advantages of such investments and on the other the risks that we face. It is in this context that effectively we are advancing in our studies on the South Pars field," the spokesman quoted Desmarast as saying.
Total spokesman Regis Gaignault said: "This is the first time we have said that we are studying South Pars."
Gaignault quoted Desmarest saying Total would not be deterred by U.S. sanctions against dealings with Iran and this would not hinder a decision to go ahead with the project.

South Pars is an extension in Iranian waters of Qatar's North Field. The newsletter Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) said recently that the National Iranian Oil Co's (NIOC) offshore arm expected to revise estimates of the field's gas reserves to perhaps as much as 500 trillion cubic feet.

Iran said in November that it hoped to award the first of 10 oil and gas projects open to bids from international firms within the next three months. First projects likely to be awarded under the "buy-back" scheme would include South Pars.
Total signed a ground-breaking agreement with NIOC in 1995 to develop the Sirri A and E oil and gas fields.
